A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LieRE work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, UCF101, and a synthetic spatial task, alongside ablations and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports an initialization-sensitivity comparison and statistical test outcomes.

M1.justification: Both versions learn skew-symmetric bases, exponentiate position-weighted combinations, and rotate attention keys and queries. Block-size variants and parameter sharing are unchanged. The reformatted pseudocode and Python implementation do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three classification datasets and synthetic arrow task, including the same resolution, reduced-data, and patch-shuffling scenarios. The initialization analysis does not document additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and ablation comparisons retain absolute positional encoding, VisionLlama RoPE, and RoPE-Mixed. The new initialization comparison uses the existing RoPE-Mixed comparator; newly discussed related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds a comparison of initialization scales 2π and 1 in Appendix B.6/Table 7. Section 5.2 also now states that all absolute-encoding variants used 800,000 examples, conflicting with the retained 2-million-example row in Table 3. This is a reported-setting inconsistency, not evidence that the existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds an initialization-sensitivity analysis comparing LieRE8 and RoPE-Mixed. It removes v3's raw and smoothed CIFAR-100 validation-accuracy and training-loss curves (Figures 11–12). Data-size, capacity, sharing, shuffling, resolution, and attention-map analyses remain.

E5.justification: v4 supplements existing confidence intervals with baseline-comparison p-values in Table 2 and paired Z-tests, mean differences, and confidence intervals for initialization effects in Table 7. v3 already reported 95% intervals, including bootstrapped intervals. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: The matched benchmark, model-size, shuffling, FLOP, validation-loss, and basis-scaling values remain unchanged. New Table 7 reports mean differences of -0.0118 for LieRE8 and -0.0255 for RoPE-Mixed, with p-values 0.070 and 0.00012; Table 2 adds further p-values. The earlier epoch-by-epoch learning-curve results are removed.

T1.justification: v4 adds Appendix A's claimed one-dimensional representational equivalence between LieRE and RoPE, with a derivation using orthogonal block diagonalization and absorption of the basis change into key/query projections. It also explains why this argument does not generally extend to multiple positional dimensions. This substantive capacity analysis has no counterpart in v3.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the advertised improvement from '2% relative' on 2D tasks and 1.5% on 3D tasks to 1.5% and 1%, dropping the explicit relative qualifier. The underlying benchmark scores and the main methodological, efficiency, and generalization claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds a possible dataset-size explanation for model-scaling behavior when training from scratch (Appendix B.5), and distinguishes one-dimensional from higher-dimensional capacity in Appendix A. The new scaling discussion names ViT-Huge even though Table 6 retains ViT-Large. The architecture and pose-encoding limitations in Section 7 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the general code-release statement with an explicit StanfordMIMI/LieRE repository link in the abstract. The detailed hardware, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and implementation disclosures are otherwise retained; reformatting the Python listing does not establish a different implementation.

R1.justification: New Sections 2.3–2.5 substantially broaden positioning beyond positional encodings and RoPE extensions. They discuss efficient multidimensional architectures such as Axial Attention, Perceiver, and VMamba; equivariant networks such as SE(3)-Transformers and Equiformer; and other applications of Lie groups, with corresponding new references.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main-section sequence remain intact. v4 makes localized wording corrections, renames Section 5.4 to LieRE Capacity, reorganizes appendix headings, replaces Broader Impacts with an Impact statement, and updates affiliations and acknowledgements. This is not an extensive rewrite of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v4 combines the two pseudocode figures into Figure 3, moves the model-size plot from the main text to Appendix B.5, adds two statistical tables, removes the two learning-curve figures, and reformats the code listing. Figure 1's caption is revised, while retained benchmark graphics preserve their plotted content and the overall layout style remains.

improvement.justification: v4 makes initialization sensitivity more assessable through Table 7, where v3 only noted it, and improves research positioning and code-access guidance. These provide a limited net gain. The principal benchmark evidence is unchanged, while removal of convergence curves reduces supporting detail and the new 800,000-example statement conflicts with the retained 2-million-example control, limiting the improvement in reporting quality.
